buckets.title: Hybridisation, sigma/pi overlap and molecular shape
buckets.badge_reason: Most items require a short conceptual or representational bridge rather than formula execution.

scope.covers: Introductory localized hybrid-orbital descriptions for the supplied BF3/NH3, H2CO, ethene, CO2, CH3F, HCN, methylamine and CH4/NH3/H2O cases.
excluded: Delocalised molecular-orbital treatments, hypervalent models, radicals and amide resonance beyond the supplied questions.

microtopics.title: Domain count before hybridisation label
microtopics.badge_reason: The key error is a model-selection shortcut: sigma-bond count is substituted for full electron-domain count.
microtopics.inferential_jump: A sigma-bond count is not the local domain count when lone pairs are present; choose the introductory hybrid model only after the full domain inventory.

teaching_path.action: Separate sigma-bond count from total local electron-domain count.
teaching_path.why_valid: Lone pairs occupy local electron-density regions even though they are not sigma bonds.

teaching_path.action: Inventory bond directions and lone-pair domains before choosing the introductory hybrid label.
teaching_path.why_valid: The introductory mapping is keyed to regions/directions, not merely the number of bonded atoms.

teaching_path.action: Check the proposed label against the electron-domain geometry and note that shape is model evidence, not direct orbital measurement.
teaching_path.why_valid: This prevents a shape-only proof claim.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Three sigma bonds always imply the same local hybridisation.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: What changes in the central-domain count when a lone pair is present?
misconceptions.repair: Count every local electron-density direction, including lone pairs; a multiple bond still occupies one direction.

exit_task.prompt: Two centres each have three sigma bonds; one also has a lone pair. What must you count before deciding whether their introductory local models match?

answer.summary: Count total local electron domains, not sigma bonds alone.
reasoning: The lone pair occupies an additional domain.
The introductory model follows the full local domain count.
answer.check: Recount the regions directly from the Lewis descriptions.

microtopics.title: Sigma/pi orbital inventory without double-counting
microtopics.badge_reason: The learner must translate between Lewis domains and a 3D orbital-overlap representation while preserving two different counting systems.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Build the sigma-direction frame first, then allocate only the remaining unhybridised p orbital(s) to pi overlap; never count a pi component as a new sigma/domain direction.

teaching_path.action: Keep the domain-direction ledger separate from the sigma/pi bond-component ledger.
teaching_path.why_valid: A multiple bond is one local direction even though it contains more than one bond component.

teaching_path.action: Construct the hybrid sigma framework from the local domain count, then identify the unhybridised p orbital(s) left over.
teaching_path.why_valid: Hybridisation changes the basis used for the sigma framework while leaving specific p directions available for pi overlap.

teaching_path.action: Orient remaining p orbitals for side-on overlap: perpendicular to an sp2 molecular plane, or as two independent p directions around an sp linear axis.
teaching_path.why_valid: Pi overlap requires parallel p orbitals and is geometrically distinct from sigma overlap along the axis.

teaching_path.action: Close the inventory by checking each local valence orbital has one assigned role and each multiple bond has exactly one sigma component.
teaching_path.why_valid: This catches double-counting and domain/component conflation.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A pi bond is an extra electron-domain direction or can reuse a sigma hybrid orbital.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: After the sigma framework is allocated, which local atomic orbitals remain unused?
misconceptions.repair: Give each local orbital one bonding job: hybrid directions support the sigma framework and separate unhybridised p orbitals support side-on pi overlap.

exit_task.prompt: A three-domain carbon has a sigma framework and one pi participation. Sketch the local orbital jobs without naming a molecule.

answer.summary: Use three coplanar sigma-framework hybrid directions and one separate perpendicular p direction for pi participation.
reasoning: Reserve the remaining p orbital for side-on overlap.
answer.check: Tick each local orbital exactly once against a bonding job.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The exit task checks a qualitative chemical-model correspondence.

microtopics.title: Electron-domain geometry versus molecular shape
microtopics.badge_reason: The same all-domain geometry can project to different atom-only shapes when lone-pair occupancy changes.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Electron-domain geometry names all local regions; molecular shape names bonded-atom positions, so lone pairs can change the latter without changing the former.

teaching_path.action: Name electron-domain geometry and molecular shape as different projections.
teaching_path.why_valid: One includes all regions; the other records atom positions.

teaching_path.action: Mark bond versus lone-pair occupancy on the common domain scaffold.
teaching_path.why_valid: Changing occupancy changes which vertices are occupied by atoms.

teaching_path.action: Check CH4, NH3 and H2O as 0/1/2-lone-pair cases with four total domains.
teaching_path.why_valid: A shared total domain count with different atom subsets is a direct counterexample to conflating the names.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Tetrahedral electron-domain geometry means the bonded atoms must form a tetrahedron.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Which domain positions contain atoms and which contain lone pairs?
misconceptions.repair: Keep the tetrahedral all-domain scaffold, then derive molecular shape from only the bonded-atom positions.

exit_task.prompt: Four central domains contain three bonds and one lone pair. Which geometry description still counts four positions, and what does the atom-only shape count?

answer.summary: Electron-domain geometry retains all four positions; molecular shape follows the three bonded atoms.
reasoning: Lone-pair occupancy does not remove a domain.
It does remove that position from the atom-only shape.
answer.check: Count total domains and bonded atoms separately.

solution_structure: Allocate remaining p orbital(s) to pi overlap and close the orbital inventory.

safe_variations: Use three-domain or two-domain centres while preserving the allocation rule.
transfer_boundaries: This is an introductory localized valence-bond model, not a claim that shape alone measures orbital mixing.
common_wrong_routes: Count pi components as extra domain directions or reuse a hybrid orbital for a pi job.

items.title: Close an orbital inventory under a changed local description
items.prompt: A neutral carbon centre is described by three coplanar sigma-bond directions and one perpendicular p-orbital participation. Without using a memorised molecule name, give an orbital-job inventory and state one check that would expose double-counting.
items.source_label: Original transfer task; not claimed as an official exam/PYQ item.

answer.summary: Three sigma-framework hybrid directions and one separate p-orbital pi job; check that each local valence orbital is allocated once.
reasoning: The three sigma directions define the local sigma framework.
The perpendicular p direction is reserved for side-on pi overlap.
A closure check prevents any orbital from being assigned twice.

items.title: Hold domain geometry fixed while changing atom occupancy
items.prompt: A four-domain centre is changed from four bonds to two bonds plus two lone pairs without changing the total domain count. Explain which geometry description is preserved and which atom-only description must be reconsidered.

answer.summary: The four-domain electron geometry stays tetrahedral; the molecular shape must be derived from the two bonded-atom positions.
